Answer: B
Reason: Comparing the initial chest X-ray (Figure 1a) with the follow-up image (Figure 4), there is a clear progression of the opacity in the right lung, which has become denser and more extensive. Additionally, new patchy opacities have appeared in the left lung. This pattern of progressive consolidation spreading to other lobes or lungs is characteristic of invasive adenocarcinoma (formerly known as bronchioloalveolar carcinoma).
